title: In vivo and In vitro Rearing of Entomopathogenic Nematodes (Steinernematidae and Heterorhabditidae)
protocol: Invert a 100 x 15 mm plastic Petri dish.
Place two discs of filter paper (90 mm) in the lid of the dish.
Evenly distribute 1 ml of the IJ water suspension on the filter paper.
Add 10 last instar larvae of the greater waxmoth Galleria mellonella to the dish.
Cover the lid with the bottom of the Petri dish.
Label the Petri dish with nematode species name, isolate code/designation, and date infection trap was set.
Place the dish inside a loosely sealed plastic bag.
Keep the dish in the dark at room temperature or in an incubator between 20-25 °C.
Check dishes daily.
Remove cadavers with signs of nematode infection to a modified White trap after 3-5 days.
Chop liver and kidney into small pieces (2 cm³ or smaller).
Place chopped tissue into a blender with NaCl, agar, and 300 ml of water.
Blend the mixture until it becomes a liquid pulp, thick paste, or puree.
Transfer the blended mixture to a 1 L Erlenmeyer flask.
Add the final 200 ml of water to the blender vessel.
Decant any remaining media into the Erlenmeyer flask.
Autoclave the mixture for 15 min at 121 °C.
Allow agar to cool to touch before pouring.
Pour approximately 20 ml of agar onto 5 (or 6) cm Petri dishes while hand stirring or swirling the Erlenmeyer flask between pours.
Use a flame-sterilized metal spatula to break up any large chunks of meat poured into the Petri dish.
Prepare lipid agar medium by mixing nutrient broth, agar, and yeast extract in a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask.
Add distilled H₂O and MgCl₂•6H₂O to the mixture.
Autoclave for 15 min at 121 °C.
Sterilize corn oil and syrup using a UV cross-linker.
Pour approximately 20 ml of agar onto a 5 (or 6) cm Petri dish after adding sterilized corn oil and syrup mix.
Allow the agar to solidify before storing dishes at 4 °C until needed.
Streak the desired symbiotic bacteria onto the lipid agar plate.
Incubate plates at 28 °C for 24-48 hours.
Spread 100-200 μl of overnight (12-16 hour) LB subculture on the plate.
Add approximately 0.4 ml of surface sterilized nematode suspension to the plate.
Incubate plates at room temperature in the dark or in an incubator at 22 ±3 °C.
Monitor cultures daily for nematode growth.
Transfer bottom dish with agar when nematodes are seen crawling the sides of the dish.
Harvest IJs using a modified White trap under a laminar flow hood.
Rinse IJ suspension to remove any medium debris.
Store IJs in sterilized distilled water at 10 °C or use immediately if needed.
Infect 10-20 G. mellonella larvae with IJs of the desired nematode species.
Collect cadavers after 3 or 4 days when IJs have matured to first generation adults.
Infect more G. mellonella larvae if necessary and start dissections as early as the 48 hr post-infection to assess developmental stage.
Place each cadaver individually in a Petri dish with saline solution (M9 buffer).
Dissect a cadaver by pulling its head with a fine tip forceps.
Collect at least 20 gravid females with a fine needle and place them in a watch glass containing 10 ml of M9 buffer.
Prepare an axenizing solution using distilled water, 5 N NaOH, and diluted bleach solution.
Rinse females at least three times with M9 buffer filling the watch glass with buffer solution and sucking up buffer with a pipette.
Add the axenizing solution immediately.
Allow females to remain in the axenizing solution for no more than 10–15 minutes.
Manually disrupt female bodies using a needle or scalpel to speed up tissue disintegration.
Pipette intact eggs into 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes, avoiding undissolved tissues.
Vortex tubes for 15 seconds at high speed setting or pipet up and down several times if vortex is unavailable.
Pellet eggs by centrifugation at approximately 18,000 g for 2 minutes; increase speed if necessary.
Remove axenizing solution and rinse eggs twice with sterile distilled water by centrifuging at 900 x g for 1 minute.
Resuspend eggs in 300–500 µl of sterile distilled water after the last wash.
Place resuspended eggs in a sterile 3 cm Petri dish or sterilized watch glass.
Examine eggs under a dissecting microscope at 30-50X magnification to confirm they are intact.
Transfer confirmed intact eggs to a 5 cm plate with liver-kidney agar.
Do not add more than 400 µl of the egg suspension on the plates.
Label plates with appropriate information and store them upright in the dark at 28 °C.
Observe dishes periodically for hatching of eggs overnight.
Place the dish in a plastic bag to retain moisture after condensation evaporation.
Discard any dishes showing signs of fungal or bacterial contamination.
Remove the lid when IJs are seen migrating up the wall of the Petri dish.
Transfer the bottom dish with agar into a modified White trap under sterile conditions.
Continue monitoring the White Traps and harvest IJ as needed.
